news.title: Uefa has formed a rare but fragile united front against Fifa in battle for football’s future | Nick Ames and Matt Hughes
news.lede: Emerging from this week with unity over Fifa’s World Cup sell off was quite an acheivement but Europe cannot rest on its laurels. It was a phrase not always heard when Europe’s football associations discuss a pressing issue. “Touchingly unanimous,” was the assessment of a senior Uefa executive within moments of Thursday afternoon’s seismic decision to boycott Fifa tournaments unless Gianni Infantino scraps his private investment plan. United fronts on this scale are vanishingly rare and there is now a narrow window in which to make it count.

news.title: Gianni Infantino’s World Cup plan receives crucial update amid boycott fears as FIFA insists ‘nobody is sel...
news.lede: Gianni Infantino’s latest proposal has triggered one of the biggest governance battles in modern soccer, with growing boycott threats and fierce opposition from several continental confederations. As the dust settles following the 2026 World Cup, the governing body has now provided a significant update, despite mounting criticism and fears that future tournaments could be affected. The controversy has quickly evolved into a global debate over the future of the sport. While several federations believe the proposal could permanently alter the sport’s biggest competition, FIFA argues that every member association deserves the opportunity to study the plan before making a decision.

news.title: Six Argentina players could be banned from next World Cup as FIFA issues response
news.lede: The team was at the centre of several controveries during the World Cup. FIFA has confirmed disciplinary proceedings against six members of the Argentinian national team, meaning that they could be barred from the 2030 World Cup. The Argentinian side was at the centre of a number of controversies during the course of the tournament, including criticism of their conduct during matches, as well as on the field afterwards. Argentina ultimately lost out to Spain in the final, with Spain scoring in extra time after a tense match, resulting in a 1-0 victory.

news.title: How does MLS pick up the World Cup mantle? Casemiro helps, but it’ll take much more
news.lede: The World Cup gave MLS unprecedented momentum. Keeping it will depend less on signing aging icons than convincing America’s best young players to stay. “Thanks World, we’ll take it from here,” is Major League Soccer’s message to the American public. Yet two moves in the last week were emblematic of the issues the league faces in taking on the mantle of North America’s hosting of the game’s grandest stage.

news.title: UEFA to boycott World Cup if Infantino sell-off plan goes ahead
news.lede: This content is provided by Exco Player and may use cookies or similar technologies. Please click 'Allow and Continue' below to load the content. England, its fellow UEFA nations and CONCACAF have unanimously voted to boycott the upcoming men’s and women’s World Cups if Gianni Infantino goes ahead with plans to sell off shares in the tournament to private investors. UEFA’s 55 member nations held a virtual crisis meeting on Thursday to discuss Infantino’s recently announced plans to privatise and sell shares in the World Cup.
